sources.requirement: Doctors must meet the recertification programme requirements set by Council; vocational scope must participate in the recertification programme offered by their medical college; general scope via a college programme or the Inpractice programme. Council 'has recently strengthened' vocational requirements; providers to implement by 1 July 2022.

Core elements for vocationally-registered doctors: mix of activities across three CPD categories (1 Reviewing and reflecting on practice; 2 Measuring and improving outcomes; 3 Educational activities/CME); structured conversation with a peer, colleague or employer at least annually; professional development plan (PDP). 'Cultural safety and a focus on health equity must be embedded within all of the above activities.' No hours stated in this document; no te reo requirement.

Recertification programme must provide a process of 'at least 50 hours each year' covering Council domains of competence; at least one medical audit per year; peer review minimum 10 hours per year. Document is an older college reaccreditation standard, date not found in extracted text; it still uses 'cultural competence' wording, so treat as possibly superseded in detail.

General scope, Inpractice programme, over 12 months: professional development plan; 20 hours CME; 10 hours peer review; one medical audit; four meetings with nominated collegial relationship provider. Page does not mention cultural safety or te reo, and does not itself state a 50 hour total.

Accreditation standards effective 1 July 2022: colleges must embed cultural safety and a focus on health equity across the three CPD categories (refers to Statement on cultural safety and He Ara Hauora Maori). No te reo or Maori language requirement for individual doctors found in the text.

Te Whanake CPD (triennium): annual essentials = record goals for each learning category plus one structured annual conversation with a peer/colleague/employer; minimum 96 learning credits per triennium (1 credit = 1 learning hour, with stated exceptions) with minimum 12 in each of 4 categories: Medical Education, Cultural Safety and Equity, Patient Outcomes, Reviewing Practice; minimum 12 reflection credits per triennium; valid ACLS resuscitation certificate every 3 years for Fellows. DRHM/Dual Fellows: 120 clinical attachment hours per triennium. No te reo requirement in the policy.
sources.asOf: policy CO-A-001-03 approved Dec 2023, effective Jan 2024, review Dec 2026

sources.requirement: Credit schedule by active months: 12 months 17 total credits; 24 months 56; 36 months 96. Reflections/each-category minimum: 1 at 15 months, 5 at 18-24, 6 at 27-30, 9 at 33, 12 at 36. Categories ME, RP, CSE, PO.

Programme page: minimum 96 credits over triennium across four learning categories; reflections; annual goal setting; annual structured conversation. No Maori health hours or te reo stated. A 2017 RNZCGP document (https://www.rnzcgp.org.nz/gpdocs/New-website/Dashboard/Resources/CPD-Resources/2017-Activities-for-cultural-competence-requirements.pdf) was seen in search results only (NOT fetched): reported as recognising reo/tikanga Maori courses for the old cultural competence requirement. Not verified, not a current mandate.

2026 CPD Framework: minimum 50 hours; Category 1 Educational Activities min 12.5 h; Categories 2 (Reviewing Performance) + 3 (Measuring Outcomes) min 25 h combined, at least 5 h each; remaining 12.5 h any category; minimum 2 activities on cultural safety and addressing health inequities, and 2 on ethics and professional behaviour, annually. No NZ-specific Maori health hours or te reo requirement stated.

2026 CPD Program: minimum 50 hours annually; PDP 2h; formal peer review min 10h; practice improvement min 5h; self-guided learning 12.5h; additional 12.5h; CAPE domains include Culturally safe practice and Addressing health inequities (page sets no minimum hours for them). MCNZ sets NZ CPD requirements. No te reo requirement. Table text garbled on fetch; breakdown is best reading.

One hour of te reo Maori per year for NZ doctors: NOT FOUND in any MCNZ, RNZCGP, RACP or RANZCP source checked, and a domain-restricted search of those four sites found nothing. Health NZ / employer policy was not checked from primary sources (not found).
